items.followUp: Differentiate between linear motion and rotatory motion.

rubric.why: One mark for describing circular motion as motion along a circular path about an external point or axis.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the body moves along a circular path around an external point or axis.

rubric.why: One mark for distinguishing rotatory motion by its axis of rotation through the body.
rubric.description: Defines rotatory motion and distinguishes it from circular motion.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the body spins about an axis passing through it.

modelAnswer: In circular motion, an object moves along a circular path around an external point or axis.
In rotatory motion, a body spins about an axis passing through itself.

items.followUp: State one difference between circular motion and rotatory motion, and give one example of each.

rubric.why: One mark for naming two valid methods of reducing friction.
rubric.description: Gives two methods of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Award for any two correct methods, such as lubrication, polishing surfaces, or using ball bearings.

rubric.why: One mark for naming two further valid methods of reducing friction.
rubric.description: Gives two further methods of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Award for any two correct methods; accept methods beyond the examples in the first point.

modelAnswer: Friction can be reduced by applying lubricants and by polishing the surfaces.
It can also be reduced by using ball bearings and by streamlining objects moving through fluids.

items.followUp: Explain why a vehicle is less likely to skid on a banked road when moving at the designed speed.

rubric.why: One mark for identifying the raised outer edge of the road.
rubric.description: Describes how the road is banked.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the outer edge of the road is raised above the inner edge.

rubric.why: One mark for explaining how banking helps provide the centripetal force and reduce the risk of skidding.
rubric.description: Explains why banking makes turning safer.
rubric.how: Award for connecting the road's normal reaction (or its horizontal component) with the centripetal force needed for turning.

modelAnswer: On a banked road, the outer edge is raised above the inner edge.
The horizontal component of the normal reaction provides the centripetal force needed for turning, reducing reliance on friction and the risk of skidding.

items.followUp: What is an ideal rigid body?

rubric.why: One mark for identifying the body as one whose shape and size do not change.
rubric.description: States that a rigid body does not deform.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its shape and size remain unchanged when forces act on it.

rubric.why: One mark for giving the defining constant-distance condition.
rubric.description: States the condition for a rigid body.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the distance between any two particles or points of the body remains constant.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body whose shape and size do not change when a force acts on it.
The distance between any two particles of a rigid body remains constant.

items.followUp: Write the formula for the gravitational potential energy of a body and identify its symbols.

rubric.why: One mark for defining potential energy in terms of position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award for stating that potential energy is stored energy due to a body's position or configuration.

rubric.why: One mark for the correct mathematical formula.
rubric.description: Gives the formula for gravitational potential energy.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.
For a body at height h, its gravitational potential energy is PE = mgh.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a solar cell and a solar panel?

rubric.why: One mark for describing a solar cell as a device that converts sunlight into electrical energy.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a solar cell converts sunlight directly into electricity.

rubric.why: One mark for explaining that a panel is made from multiple solar cells.
rubric.description: Distinguishes a solar panel from a single cell.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a solar panel consists of many solar cells connected together.

modelAnswer: A solar cell is a device that converts sunlight directly into electrical energy.
A solar panel consists of many solar cells connected together.

items.followUp: A machine does 30 J of work in 5 s. Calculate its power.

rubric.why: One mark for identifying the work and time from the question in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for identifying W = 4 J and t = 2 s.

rubric.why: One mark for using the power formula and obtaining the correct answer with its unit.
rubric.how: Award for using P = W/t and giving P = 2 W.

modelAnswer: Given: Work done, W = 4 J; time, t = 2 s.

items.followUp: State Pascal's law and name one device that uses it.

rubric.why: One mark for stating that the law concerns pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.description: Identifies the applied pressure in Pascal's law.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning pressure applied to an enclosed or confined fluid.

rubric.why: One mark for stating that the pressure is transmitted equally and undiminished throughout the fluid.
rubric.description: States how the pressure is transmitted.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the applied pressure is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions through the fluid and to the container walls.

modelAnswer: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions throughout the fluid and to the walls of its container.
